scope: Sources and fixtures come from the independently versioned OpenMS4-cli, OpenMS4-topp and OpenMS4-test-data packages; the algorithm the tool calls (MSExperiment::updateRanges and getMaxIntensity) is resolved against the pinned Core SDK checkout at core bc9cc12.
method: Tool transcribed from the pinned C++. The upstream invocation is reproduced against the retained C++ output and compared canonically: the upstream ${DIFF} runs with an index whitelist, so byte equality was never the contract. The two chromatogram-scale cases are executed against the pinned C++ Release build (see external_reference_artifacts), the degenerate intensity ranges -- empty, all-zero, all-negative -- are executed against it as well rather than reasoned from the source, and the whole fix is verified on the 1.2 GB benchmark input.
evidence_tier: executed differential (tier 1), canonical comparison against retained C++ tool output, plus a full-size executed comparison on real instrument data

source_anchors.operation: main_: exp.updateRanges(); double max = exp.getMaxIntensity() / 100.0; then every MS1 peak intensity is divided by max. Nothing narrows the maximum to the spectra.

MSExperiment::updateRanges(): clears the range managers, extends spectrum_ranges_ from every spectrum at every MS level, extends chromatogram_ranges_ from every chromatogram, then combined_ranges_.extendUnsafe(spectrum_ranges_) followed by combined_ranges_.extendUnsafe(chromatogram_ranges_). The combined intensity maximum therefore includes chromatogram points.
double getMaxIntensity() const { return combined_ranges_.getMaxIntensity(); } -- the combined range, not the spectrum range.

RangeBase::getMax(): `if (isEmpty()) { throw Exception::InvalidRange(..., "Empty or uninitialized range object. Did you forget to call updateRanges()?"); } return max_;` -- an unconditional throw, not behind OPENMS_ASSERTIONS, so a Release build throws too. RangeIntensity::getMaxIntensity() (line 455) forwards to it, and MSExperiment::getMaxIntensity() (MSExperiment.h:1059) forwards to that. MapNormalizer.cpp:94 asks for it one line before the peak loop, so an empty combined intensity range refuses the run whether or not the loop body would have run.

indexed mzML trailer: os << "<fileChecksum>"; then `// TODO calculate checksum here: SHA-1 checksum from beginning of file to end of 'fileChecksum' open tag.` and std::string sha1_checksum = "0". The C++ writer emits the literal 0 for every indexed mzML; the port's real SHA-1 is the conforming side. Recorded here because MapNormalizer writes an indexed mzML on both sides.

target_verification.tests: tests/topp_map_normalizer.rs, five cases: the upstream invocation, the two chromatogram-scale cases against executed C++ output, the empty-combined-intensity-range refusal on both of its shapes, and the parameter/format refusals; plus three private tests in src/cli/tools/map_normalizer.rs for the derived work ceiling, the combined maximum and the refused empty run
target_verification.deliberate_deviation: Exactly one, and it is not the empty range. Both sides REFUSE a run whose combined intensity range is empty and both write no output file; only the exit code differs, C++ 8 (its InvalidRange reaches TOPPBase's UNKNOWN_ERROR arm) against this port's 6, because Error::InvalidValue and Error::InvalidRange map to ILLEGAL_PARAMETERS crate-wide -- the mapping documented at run_failure in src/cli.rs, not a choice this tool makes. The deviation proper is the non-positive scale: executed, the C++ exits 0 and writes NaN (all-zero run) or sign-flipped intensities (all-negative run), where this port refuses with exit 6 and writes nothing. See ../oracle/map-normalizer-divergence/degenerate.log.
target_verification.cpp_issue_candidate: Two, both in the C++ and both disclosed rather than worked around here. (1) MapNormalizer divides by getMaxIntensity()/100 with no guard. Executed at the pinned Release build: an all-zero run exits 0 with NaN in every MS1 peak, and an all-negative run exits 0 with every MS1 peak sign-flipped and scaled by 100 (maximum -1.00, so the scale is -0.01); this port refuses a non-positive scale with exit 6. The neighbouring empty-range case is NOT part of this candidate: there the C++ refuses cleanly, exit 8, and so does the port. (2) MzMLHandlerHelper::writeFooter writes <fileChecksum>0</fileChecksum> with a TODO instead of the SHA-1 the indexedmzML schema asks for; the port writes the real digest, which is the conforming behaviour and costs it a full pass over the output.
target_verification.port_issue_reported: SummaryLimits::default().max_work is a fixed 50,000,000 units, where MSExperiment::combined_ranges, chromatogram_ranges and calculate_tic_binned charge one unit per spectrum, per peak, per chromatogram and per chromatogram point. The benchmark's 1.2 GB Velos run charges 88,521,983, so combined_ranges() refuses it; the port's mzML reader admits that file, so the ceiling refuses data the reader already read. MapNormalizer derives its own ceiling from the materialised map (MapNormalizer::range_limits) and does not change the shared default, which belongs to src/kernel/experiment_summary.rs.
